name: Virginia
note: In Virginia the funeral director (or next of kin) who first takes custody of the body completes the death certificate and files it within three days, before disposition; funeral directors must file through the Electronic Death Registration System straight to the State Registrar, while next of kin may file on paper with a district registrar. The physician or autonomous nurse practitioner files the medical certification electronically within 24 hours, and the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner takes violent, sudden, unattended and custodial deaths. Onward, the State Registrar sends the Department of Elections a weekly electronic list of decedents for voter-roll cancellation, from July 2027 supplemented by an annual match against the SSA death list. Certified copies are limited to surviving relatives and legal representatives, a class the regulations extend to the decedent's life insurer, and the DMV can issue them; death records become public after 25 years.

steps.title: Pronounce death
steps.who: A physician or autonomous nurse practitioner; or a registered nurse, physician assistant or non-autonomous APRN working for a home care organisation, hospice, hospital, nursing home, the Department of Corrections or a continuing care retirement community, under the statutory criteria.
steps.trigger: Absence of spontaneous respiratory and cardiac function (or, by a qualified physician, brain death).
steps.summary: Nurses and PAs may pronounce in defined settings but may not determine the cause, which stays with the attending physician or autonomous nurse practitioner. If the death was not anticipated or needs a medical examiner investigation, they must notify the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner and may not release the body to the funeral director.

steps.title: Notify the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner
steps.who: The physician in attendance, hospital, law-enforcement officer, funeral director, or any other person with knowledge of the death.
steps.trigger: Death from trauma, injury, violence, poisoning, accident, suicide or homicide; sudden death in apparent good health; death unattended by a physician; death in jail, prison or police custody or a state hospital or training center; sudden infant death; or suspicious, unusual or unnatural death.
steps.summary: The Office of the Chief Medical Examiner takes charge of the body, investigates cause and manner of death, and reports to the Commonwealth's attorney and investigating police.

steps.title: File the medical certification through EDRS
steps.who: The physician or autonomous nurse practitioner in charge of the patient's care for the fatal illness, or the one who pronounced; in their absence or with approval, an associate, supervised PA, APRN, the facility's chief medical officer, a hospitalist, the autopsy physician, or a delegate with access to the history in a natural death.
steps.summary: The medical certification is completed and filed electronically with the State Registrar through EDRS within 24 hours. If the cause cannot be determined in that time, the funeral director is told why and disposition waits for authorisation.

steps.title: Medical examiner certifies investigated deaths
steps.who: The Chief Medical Examiner (through the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner).
steps.trigger: A death requiring OCME inquiry or investigation.

deadline.text: within 24 hours after being notified of the death

steps.summary: The Chief Medical Examiner has the cause investigated and the medical certification completed and filed within 24 hours of notification; if OCME declines jurisdiction, the last treating physician certifies.

steps.title: Funeral director files the death certificate through EDRS
steps.who: The licensed funeral director, funeral service licensee or state anatomical program that first assumes custody, with personal data (including SSN or DMV control number) from the best qualified person or source.

deadline.text: within three days after death and before final disposition or removal from the Commonwealth

steps.summary: Funeral directors must file electronically with the State Registrar through EDRS within three days and before disposition. The informant's name and relationship are entered on the certificate. Wilfully making a false statement in a certificate is a Class 4 felony.

steps.title: Next of kin may file on paper with a district registrar
steps.who: Next of kin (as defined in § 54.1-2800) who first assumes custody of the body.
steps.trigger: Taking custody of the body without a funeral director.

deadline.text: within three days after death and before final disposition

steps.summary: Where the family itself takes custody, a next of kin completes the certificate and may file it non-electronically with the registrar of any district within the same three-day limit.

steps.title: Out-of-state transit permit
steps.who: The registrar of the district where the certificate was filed.
steps.trigger: Removal of the body from Virginia.
steps.summary: A permit is needed only to take a body out of Virginia, and is issued on a satisfactorily completed death certificate; no permit is required for disposition within the Commonwealth.

steps.title: Certified copies to surviving relatives and legal representatives
steps.who: The State Registrar or a city or county registrar (district health department).
steps.trigger: A written request showing a direct and tangible interest.
steps.summary: Disclosing or copying vital records is unlawful except as authorised. Death certificates go to surviving relatives or their legal representatives, a class that for death records includes the funeral service licensee, attorney, attorney-in-fact, life insurer, acting government agency, guardian or administrator; grandchildren and great-grandchildren are also entitled by statute.

steps.title: DMV issues certified copies
steps.who: The Commissioner of the Department of Motor Vehicles, subject to the State Registrar's rules and audit.
steps.summary: Virginia's DMV is authorised to issue certified copies of death records held by the State Registrar.

steps.title: Data for national vital statistics
steps.trigger: Cost-sharing arrangements with the federal agency.
steps.summary: The federal agency responsible for national vital statistics may be furnished copies or data, for statistics, research and public-health investigation only.

steps.title: Weekly decedent list to the Department of Elections
steps.who: The State Registrar of Vital Records, to the Department of Elections; general registrars cancel.
steps.trigger: Deaths in Virginia of persons aged 17 or over since the previous list.
steps.summary: The State Registrar sends a weekly electronic list with name, address, SSN and dates and places of birth and death; general registrars must promptly cancel the registration of persons known to be deceased and notify the address on file.

steps.title: Annual match against the SSA list of deceased persons (from July 2027)
steps.trigger: Annual cycle, on or before 1 July.

deadline.text: on or before July 1 of each year

steps.summary: From 1 July 2027 the Department of Elections must also match the voter lists each year against the list of deceased persons maintained by the Social Security Administration.

steps.title: Veteran suicides reported to Veterans Services
steps.who: The State Registrar, to the Virginia Department of Veterans Services.
steps.trigger: A filed death certificate of a veteran or service member listing suicide as the manner of death.
steps.summary: Where a veteran's or service member's certificate lists suicide, the State Registrar provides that information to the Department of Veterans Services.

steps.title: Life insurer may obtain a certified copy as legal representative
steps.who: The State Registrar or city or county registrar, to the insurance company insuring the registrant.
steps.summary: Board of Health regulations count the insurer of the deceased as a legal representative entitled to a certified death certificate; commercial firms requesting lists of names are excluded.

steps.title: Copies or data for public or private agencies' official duties
steps.who: The State Registrar, on Board of Health terms.
steps.trigger: A request and a reasonable fee.
steps.summary: Federal, state, local, public or private agencies or persons may be furnished copies or data for statistical or administrative purposes, used only for the purpose requested.

steps.title: Public online index of deaths
steps.who: The State Registrar, on its website and the Library of Virginia's.
steps.summary: The State Registrar keeps a public online index naming each decedent with the date and county or city of death, public from receipt; the full death record becomes public 25 years after the death.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: Certificate filed within three days after death and before disposition; medical certification within 24 hours.

informantDuty.note: Whoever first assumes custody completes the certificate: normally the funeral director, but a next of kin may do so and file on paper.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: OCME investigates only reportable deaths; there is no review of every certificate.

electronicRegistration.note: Funeral directors and medical certifiers must file through EDRS; only a next of kin filing without a funeral director may use paper.

centralPopulationRegister.note: No population register; the State Registrar holds the vital records system.

governmentPropagation.note: Weekly electronic decedent list to the Department of Elections; Social Security notification is in the federal layer.

certificateAccess.note: Certified copies only for surviving relatives and their legal representatives (including the life insurer); records become public 25 years after death, and a name-date-place index is public at once.

privateSectorVerification.note: A life insurer may obtain the certificate as legal representative, agencies may receive data on Board terms, and anyone can search the public death index; no general verification service or duty to check.

gaps: Va. Code §§ 24.2-404 and 24.2-427 exist in contingent versions (Acts 2026, cc. 992 and 1081, cl. 3) and § 24.2-408 changes on 1 July 2027; the Code does not state the contingency, so steps cite the text common to all versions.

No Virginia statute was found requiring the DMV to cancel a deceased person's licence on notice from Vital Records, or Vital Records to notify the Department of Taxation or the Department of Medical Assistance Services; any such feeds are administrative and not sourced here.
No state statute was found requiring an EDRS feed to SSA (the SSN on the certificate is required by § 32.1-263(A)); the federal side is in us-federal.
The online death index under § 32.1-271(H) is to be built under a contract with a private genealogical company, which may also provide it to subscribers; the contract itself was not read.
Probate notice to creditors was not researched as a public-notice step.
